First-case effort and second-case effort measured comparably: [ ]. Do not claim reuse savings from an estimate.

Second-engagement falsification

Pre-register a disconfirming statement before engagement two, for example: "At the six-month review, our second comparable platform engagement took the same effort as the first and reused none of its artifacts." Adapt the scope and comparison rule before collecting outcomes, not after seeing them.

  • Engagement-one and engagement-two IDs, scope, complexity and changed assumptions: .
  • Effort/elapsed-time baseline and instrument, recorded before work: . Comparable roles and units: .
  • Meaning of "same effort", tolerance and threshold authority/provenance fixed before testing: . Do not choose a tolerance during tuning to make the claim pass.
  • Named artifacts actually carried into engagement two, exact versions, adaptation effort and usage evidence: .
  • Count of gates that changed a decision, with before/after decision IDs: . Do not substitute number of meetings or gates held.
  • Kickoff to first governed agent in production: [start/end and verified environment evidence, or not-run/not-applicable]. A sandbox demo is not production.
  • Receiving-owner unaided harness date and observed change evidence: .
  • Falsification review owner, date, instrument and result [supported / disconfirmed / inconclusive]: .

A successful second desk case proves bounded reproducibility, not six-month commercial effectiveness. Missing baseline, capacity or comparable engagement evidence keeps the wider reuse claim unproven.
